title: Royalties, bootlegs and record-company publicity
summary: Chasing royalties is foolish; the Finland trip resulted from Salazar's broadcasts, and company publicity is worth more than small royalties.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: What about - Are you going to fight for royalties for things like these?

How could you keep control of this division in Thailand, how could you know if they sell your records in Finland? Well, now we are lucky that we went to Finland, but if I never had the chance to go to Finland, how are we know that it played my music or selling my records in Finland? As a matter of fact, in account of your broadcasting and your interview that you had sent to Finland, we had the opportunity to go out there and Tito Puente to go there in account of them.
Okay, so that did result from the live recordings that I made at the Corso. So then it has been effective.
So then your advice to band leaders is, if someone wants to record you live, go ahead and do it...
.... and not to worry about the royalties?
Well, listen, if you sell two thousand records, how much you going to get? Do you think that is possible to have the publicity that all those records - they, I mean

those numbers that they record and spread out or sell bootleg, whatever, you going to pay for that publicity? Is like a lot of people say: "Machito, could you go to a lots of benefit, so and so, and so and so", and maybe you are going to appear for one thousand people, doing something for a worthy cause. You are involved with something humanitarian. All those things is belong to an artist. Is an obligation to do, that the artist makes, or you are not an artist.
In other words, you believe record companies with all the publicity that you are getting, that they are entitled to keep the royalties because of the money they are laying out up front?

Well, I see many, many, many artists that on account of the publicity at the, the record company had provided, make millions of dollars. Millions, because you could sell one-hundred-thousand copies, spread out in, let's say, in two cities and you could work in those two cities two, three times a year. If you are going to call if for $100,000.00 of royalties, how much it will be?; few thousand dollars, and I see guys they have sold half a million records distribute the whole world and making a tour for a year, all through the world, doing special appearances. Do you think you have money enough to publicize your name without a recording in that company? Maybe I am wrong, maybe I don't know what I am talking about.
No, it's an outlook because if you feel that the companies are laying out money to promote you, then
they should get something in return. It's fair, it's fair. Okay, Macho, think back now. Forty years you've been a band leader, fifty years you've been in music, have you regretted anything?
